finding_1_retention_parity.description: First-differencing retains comparable |r| for BOTH channel types
finding_1_retention_parity.implication: Differencing is NOT a blanket power-loss mechanism. Both channel types preserve ~95%+ of correlation magnitude.

finding_2_granger_asymmetry.description: Granger F-stat is order-of-magnitude lower for perplexity despite comparable |r|
finding_2_granger_asymmetry.implication: The low Granger F for perplexity is NOT caused by differencing removing signal. The raw |r| is equally high (~0.90). The low F reflects absence of LAGGED predictive structure.

finding_3_temporal_structure.description: Perplexity correlations are contemporaneous (lag≈0), diversity correlations are lagged (canary leads)
finding_3_temporal_structure.implication: Canary→perplexity is contemporaneous co-movement, not lagged causation. Canary→diversity shows genuine temporal precedence.

conclusions.reviewer_response: First-differencing retains 95% of |r| for diversity channels (n=243) and 100% for perplexity channels (n=8). This parity rules out blanket power loss. The asymmetry in Granger F-statistics (diversity median F=67.8 vs perplexity median F=11.5; within-experiment ratio 20-28x) instead reflects a structural difference: perplexity correlations peak at lag≈0 (contemporaneous, 50% of cases), while diversity correlations peak at lag<0 (canary temporally leads, 81% of cases). Granger causality tests lagged predictive power, so contemporaneous co-movement naturally produces lower F-statistics regardless of differencing.
